coverage_gaps.description: The three highest-value SK editorial sources for this cell (Trend, HNonline/Finweb, Dennik E) are all substantially paywalled, so automated full-text collection will capture only headlines and teasers.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Budget for institutional subscriptions to Trend + HN + Dennik N; in the interim, use vendor press-clipping archives ('Napisali o nas') and SITA agency copy to recover the substance of paywalled stories.

coverage_gaps.description: No systematic way found to search historical SK trade-press archives (pre-2015) for banking IT projects; only oPeniazoch.sk showed deep paginated archive structure.

coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Pair this media cell with the public-procurement/register cells for state-owned or state-adjacent institutions (SZRB, Eximbanka, NBS), and rely on media + vendor references for commercial banks.

brief: Slovakia's banking/IT trade-media landscape splits into three tiers: paywalled quality business press (Trend, HNonline/Finweb, Dennik E, SME, Forbes Slovensko) that carries the investigative tender, migration and executive-move reporting but resists automated collection; open specialist finance portals (Finsider, FinReport, oPeniazoch.sk, Peniaze.sk, Banky.sk) that reliably capture operational change — branch and ATM/vkladomat network shifts, cashless branches, sector AI/digitalisation round-ups — and are the most collectable high-yield layer; and IT/tech media (Zive.sk, TOUCHIT, ITnews.sk, TechByte, FinTechHub) plus English trade press (Finextra, FinTech Futures' dedicated Slovakia region page, The Paypers) for product launches and vendor-named announcements. The single most valuable non-obvious finding is that Slovak banks systematically do not name their IT suppliers, so the integrators do it for them: vendor 'Napisali o nas' press-clipping and reference pages (Asseco CE, Soitron, PosAm, EEA) republish paywalled trade-press articles and case studies and are the practical workaround for both the paywall and the attribution gap. SITA's per-actor tag pages and PRservis wire sit upstream of most SK media and should anchor the collection design; commercial bank procurement is private, so tender-dispute signal exists only for state-adjacent institutions and must be sourced from the register cells instead.
